---

# README Stability Policy

This project- and harness-neutral policy keeps a repository README useful as a
stable landing page instead of letting it grow into a changelog, roadmap, or
documentation catalog.

## Authority and provenance

After adoption, the project owns this policy. Cite its authority by project
owner and adoption or revision date, together with the project-owned
`<repository-root>/README_POLICY.md`. Never cite a vendor-, agent-, or
harness-specific bootstrap file as the authority. Bootstrap files may help
authors and tools discover the policy; they do not make the policy binding.

## Storage location

Store the adopting project's canonical copy as the git-tracked
`<repository-root>/README_POLICY.md`, alongside `README.md`. Keeping the policy
with the file it governs gives contributors, local hooks, and CI one
discoverable, versioned source of truth. A user-home, machine-global, or other
external copy may serve as a reusable template, but it must not replace the
project-owned repository copy. Once copied, the project-owned file is
authoritative and the origin is not an upstream. Do not automatically re-sync
from the origin; adopt later revisions only through deliberate local review.

Keep project-specific adoption metadata—owner, date, decisions, derived caps,
and local enforcement links—in a clearly fenced adoption note above the
neutral policy body. This keeps the reusable body free of project-specific and
harness-vendor-specific tokens without hiding local authority.

## Content contract

Keep only information a first-time visitor needs:

- purpose, audience, and top-level scope;
- prerequisites and one minimal verified quick start;
- stable architecture at a glance;
- links to canonical documentation, support, and contribution guidance;
- license and other essential repository-level notices.

Route changing detail elsewhere:

| Content | Canonical home |
| --- | --- |
| User-facing feature detail and examples | User guide or product manual |
| Current work, priorities, and roadmap status | Roadmap, issue tracker, or task system |
| Release history | Releases, changelog, or git history |
| Design rationale | Decision records or architecture docs |
| Exhaustive file/API/sample inventories | Generated indexes or dedicated references |
| Diagnostics and operational procedures | Troubleshooting or contributor docs |

Change the README only when its purpose, first-use path, top-level architecture,
or canonical navigation changes. Ordinary feature work should update the
canonical destination, not the README.

Before deleting or relocating apparent duplication, prove that it is genuinely
duplicated with a phrase, identity, or content probe against the intended
canonical home. If that home is already richer and maintained, delete the
README copy and retain one link. Relocate only information that is unique and
still belongs in maintained documentation.

## Routing pressure closure

Moving content out of the README is not sufficient if the destination can
become an unbounded neighboring sink. Inventory every destination named by the
README, this policy, or the guard's failure guidance. Give each route an owner,
lifecycle class, and pressure control, and follow routes transitively until
they end at a controlled terminal. An unclassified destination, routing cycle,
or chain that merely moves the same append pressure again is a failed adoption.

Classify routes as `reader_navigation` or `author_overflow`. The sets may
legitimately differ: readers may inspect immutable change history, while
authors must not be told to append new status prose there. Derive overflow
candidates from path-shaped destinations in the guard's actual emitted
guidance, not only from a hand-maintained table, and fail when an emitted hint
has no governed destination.

Use controls appropriate to the destination:

| Destination class | Required pressure control |
| --- | --- |
| Hot/live file | Derived line and byte ceilings plus overwrite, review, or staleness semantics |
| Partitioned manual or task collection | Bounded index plus per-part, file-count, and aggregate ceilings |
| Generated index | Size ceilings plus a reproducible freshness check against canonical sources |
| Append-only history | Query-first access plus a shard, rotation, or archival threshold; never a mandatory bootstrap read |
| External service | Named authority, retention/lifecycle owner, and a stable query/link contract |
| Frozen legacy record | Content identity or another write prohibition; never an overflow destination |

A legacy destination that is already too large is not exempt. Record its
current measured ceiling as debt, stop further growth there, and open a
separately owned partition/compaction task. Do not describe a measured legacy
ceiling as an ideal reusable default. Raising any destination threshold needs
the same explicit review as raising the README cap.

In one measured adoption, README status/history guidance routed overflow into
an otherwise unchecked neighboring status file. That file reached 1,547,057
bytes, and 94.7% of it was dated changelog content. The README cap had displaced
the pressure rather than removing it. A destination registry and unconditional
closure check make that failure visible before it becomes another megabyte-
scale bootstrap surface.

## Mechanical growth guard

Enforce both a line cap and a byte cap. Derive both from the landing page that
survives a deliberate review and trim, leaving only modest explicit headroom.
Do not copy example values from this policy. Never raise a cap merely to land
new content; move the detail to its canonical home. A cap increase requires an
explicit reviewed decision that the landing-page contract itself expanded.

A minimal deterministic check is:

```sh
line_cap=__DERIVED_LINE_CAP__
byte_cap=__DERIVED_BYTE_CAP__
lines=$(wc -l < README.md | tr -d ' ')
bytes=$(wc -c < README.md | tr -d ' ')
test "$lines" -le "$line_cap"
test "$bytes" -le "$byte_cap"
```

Replace both placeholders with the adopting project's reviewed values before
enabling the check. Keep it non-mutating, return nonzero with a routing hint on
failure, and run it unconditionally on every commit and CI build. Landing-page
size is a property of the resulting tree, so the guard must not short-circuit
merely because `README.md` is absent from a staged or changed-path set; this
also catches over-budget merge and revert results.

The same unconditional check must validate the routed-destination inventory
and each declared pressure control. A commit that does not touch the README can
still overgrow, unfreeze, remove, or silently retarget one of its destinations.

Line and byte checks are independent. In one real adoption, the retained README
was 141 lines yet already 10,297 bytes; a numbered prose list measured roughly
118 bytes per line while a path list measured roughly 57. A line budget alone
therefore cannot constrain prose density, and a byte budget alone cannot
constrain vertical sprawl.

## Adoption checklist

1. Add and commit `<repository-root>/README_POLICY.md` beside `README.md`.
2. Fence local owner/date, authoritative-copy, independence, decision, and cap
   metadata above the neutral policy body.
3. Prove apparent status, history, inventory, and deep-reference duplication
   against its canonical home; delete-with-link when that home is richer, and
   relocate only genuinely unique maintained content.
4. Verify the retained quick start and links.
5. Record where each excluded content class belongs, then inventory every
   actual route through a controlled terminal; reject cycles and unclassified
   neighboring sinks.
6. Give hot/live files line and byte caps; give partitioned, generated,
   historical, external, and frozen terminals the class-specific controls
   above. Treat measured legacy ceilings as debt, not examples.
7. Derive reviewed line and byte caps from the trimmed survivor with modest
   explicit headroom; do not copy illustrative values.
8. Commit the deterministic README and routing-closure check and wire it
   unconditionally into every local commit and CI build, independent of
   changed-path scope.
9. Require an explicit decision before the README cap or any routed-destination
   threshold can increase.

sources.epoch.py:
"""Stream exact committed sources into a plain same-volume filesystem fixture."""
import hashlib
import os
import posixpath
import shutil
import subprocess
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
BASE = Path(__file__).parent
REVISION = 'a2840582fc1722c29da808713d6f3c06bd42cd78'


def need(ok, cause):
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(cause)


def git(*args, input=None, environment=None):
    result = subprocess.run(['git', '--no-replace-objects', '-C', str(ROOT), *args],
                            input=input, env=environment, capture_output=True)
    need(result.returncode == 0 and not result.stderr, 'complete successful native Git result')
    return result.stdout


def scope(names):
    need(type(names) in (list, tuple) and names and len(names) == len(set(names)),
         'explicit nonempty unique recovery scope')
    for name in names:
        safe_path(name)
    return sorted(names)


def metadata(names):
    names = scope(names)
    raw = git('--literal-pathspecs', 'ls-tree', '-r', '--full-tree', '-z', REVISION, '--', *names)
    need(raw.endswith(b'\0'), 'complete native source framing')
    rows = {}
    for record in raw.split(b'\0')[:-1]:
        header, name = record.split(b'\t', 1)
        mode, kind, oid = header.decode().split(' ')
        path = name.decode()
        need(kind == 'blob' and mode in ('100644', '100755', '120000'),
             'only declared project blobs; no gitlink implementation recovery')
        safe_path(path)
        need(path not in rows, 'unique native source path')
        rows[path] = {'mode': mode, 'oid': oid}
    need(rows and all(any(path == name or path.startswith(name + '/') for name in names)
                     for path in rows), 'exact declared recovery namespaces')
    need(all(any(path == name or path.startswith(name + '/') for path in rows)
             for name in names), 'every declared recovery namespace exists')
    return raw, rows


def safe_path(path):
    parts = PurePosixPath(path).parts
    need(path and parts and '\0' not in path and not path.startswith('/') and str(PurePosixPath(path)) == path
         and all(part not in ('.', '..', '.git') for part in parts), 'contained canonical source path')


def alias_target(path, target):
    need(target and not target.startswith('/'), 'contained relative source alias')
    normalized = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), target))
    safe_path(normalized)
    return normalized


def restore(member, stream, root, expected):
    safe_path(member.name)
    row = expected.get(member.name)
    need(row is not None, 'archive source membership')
    target = root / member.name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for parent in target.parents:
        if parent == root:
            break
        need(not parent.is_symlink() and parent.stat().st_dev == ROOT.stat().st_dev,
             'plain same-volume source parent')
    need(not target.exists() and not target.is_symlink(), 'unique recovered source endpoint')
    if member.issym():
        need(row['mode'] == '120000', 'source alias mode')
        alias_target(member.name, member.linkname)
        raw = member.linkname.encode()
        oid = hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest()
        need(oid == row['oid'], 'whole source blob identity')
        target.symlink_to(member.linkname)
    else:
        need(member.isfile() and row['mode'] in ('100644', '100755'), 'regular source mode')
        digest = hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(member.size).encode() + b'\0')
        count = 0
        with target.open('xb') as output:
            while block := stream.read(1_048_576):
                output.write(block)
                digest.update(block)
                count += len(block)
        need(count == member.size and digest.hexdigest() == row['oid'], 'whole source blob identity')
        target.chmod(0o755 if row['mode'] == '100755' else 0o644)


def recover(root, rows, names):
    need(root.is_dir() and not root.is_symlink() and root.stat().st_dev == ROOT.stat().st_dev
         and root == root.resolve() and root.is_relative_to(ROOT / '.artifacts') and not list(root.iterdir()),
         'empty plain owned same-volume fixture root')
    names = scope(names)
    selected = dict(rows)
    need(selected and all(any(path == name or path.startswith(name + '/') for name in names)
                         for path in selected), 'exact declared recovery namespaces')
    for path, row in selected.items():
        safe_path(path)
        need(row['mode'] in ('100644', '100755', '120000'), 'declared recovery source kind')
    command = ['git', '--no-replace-objects', '--literal-pathspecs', '-C', str(ROOT),
               'archive', '--format=tar', REVISION, '--', *names]
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    observed = set()
    try:
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=process.stdout, mode='r|') as archive:
            for member in archive:
                if member.isdir():
                    safe_path(member.name.rstrip('/'))
                    continue
                need(member.name not in observed, 'unique archive source member')
                restore(member, archive.extractfile(member) if member.isfile() else None, root, selected)
                observed.add(member.name)
        error = process.stderr.read()
        need(process.wait() == 0 and not error, 'complete successful source archive')
    finally:
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.kill()
            process.wait()
        process.stdout.close()
        process.stderr.close()
    need(observed == set(selected), 'complete recovered source population')
    for path, row in selected.items():
        if row['mode'] == '120000':
            endpoint = alias_target(path, os.readlink(root / path))
            need(endpoint in selected and selected[endpoint]['mode'] in ('100644', '100755'),
                 'source alias joins an owned regular canonical source')
    return selected


def environment(root):
    need(root.is_dir() and root == root.resolve() and root.is_relative_to(ROOT / '.artifacts')
         and root.stat().st_dev == ROOT.stat().st_dev, 'plain owned same-volume Git fixture root')
    directory = root / '.artifacts'
    need(not directory.exists() and not directory.is_symlink(), 'fresh plain fixture metadata directory')
    directory.mkdir()
    index = directory / 'epoch.index'
    metadata_root = git('rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir').decode().strip()
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_DIR=metadata_root, GIT_WORK_TREE=str(root),
               GIT_INDEX_FILE=str(index), GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS='0', GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH='1',
               PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
    # This writes only the explicitly owned alternative index. Original refs,
    # configuration, objects and the primary index remain read-only.
    git('read-tree', REVISION, environment=env)
    binary = shutil.which('git')
    need(binary is not None, 'installed Git executable')
    wrapper = directory / 'readonly-bin'
    wrapper.mkdir()
    shutil.copyfile(BASE / 'git_readonly.py', wrapper / 'git')
    (wrapper / 'git').chmod(0o755)
    env.update(FSMGEN_EPOCH_ROOT=str(root), FSMGEN_EPOCH_GIT_BINARY=binary,
               PATH=str(wrapper) + os.pathsep + env['PATH'])
    return env

"""Qualify explicit source recovery and fixture Git without whole-tree copying."""
import base64
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import epoch

ROOT, BASE = epoch.ROOT, epoch.BASE
NAMES = ('README_POLICY.md', 'docs/book/src/reference-source/README_POLICY.markdown.source.txt',
         'scripts/check_docs_relative_paths.sh')
SOURCES = ('epoch.py', 'git_readonly.py', 'qualify.py', 'verify.py')


def identity(raw):
    return {'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}


def primary():
    directory = Path(epoch.git('rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir').decode().strip())
    return {'files': {name: identity((directory / name).read_bytes()) if (directory / name).exists() else None
                      for name in ('index', 'config', 'HEAD', 'packed-refs')},
            'refs': epoch.git('for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)').decode()}


def run(args, root, env):
    result = subprocess.run(args, cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return {'arguments': args, 'status': result.returncode,
            'stdout': result.stdout, 'stderr': result.stderr}


def main():
    before = primary()
    metadata, rows = epoch.metadata(NAMES)
    objects = {row['oid']: base64.b64encode(epoch.git('cat-file', 'blob', row['oid'])).decode()
               for row in rows.values()}
    controls = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='coordinate-epoch-preparation-', dir=ROOT / '.artifacts') as temporary:
        root = Path(temporary)
        epoch.recover(root, rows, NAMES)
        recovered = {}
        for path, row in rows.items():
            endpoint = root / path
            raw = os.readlink(endpoint).encode() if endpoint.is_symlink() else endpoint.read_bytes()
            assert raw == base64.b64decode(objects[row['oid']])
            recovered[path] = {'identity': identity(raw), 'mode': row['mode'],
                               'same_volume': endpoint.lstat().st_dev == ROOT.stat().st_dev,
                               'executable': bool(endpoint.lstat().st_mode & 0o111)}
        blocked = root / 'blocked'
        blocked.mkdir()
        (root / '.artifacts').symlink_to('blocked', target_is_directory=True)
        try:
            epoch.environment(root)
        except ValueError as error:
            blocked_control = {'name': 'fixture-metadata-alias', 'cause': str(error)}
        else:
            raise ValueError('false-green fixture metadata alias')
        assert not list(blocked.iterdir())
        (root / '.artifacts').unlink()
        blocked.rmdir()
        env = epoch.environment(root)
        positives = [run(args, root, env) for args in (
            ['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'],
            ['git', 'show', epoch.REVISION + ':README_POLICY.md'],
            ['git', 'ls-files', '--stage', '-z', '--', *NAMES],
            ['git', '-C', 'docs/book', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'])]
        ignored = subprocess.run(['git', 'check-ignore', '--no-index', '--stdin'], input='\n'.join(NAMES) + '\n',
                                 cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        positives.append({'arguments': ['git', 'check-ignore', '--no-index', '--stdin'],
                          'status': ignored.returncode, 'stdout': ignored.stdout, 'stderr': ignored.stderr})
        for args in (['git', 'add', 'README_POLICY.md'], ['git', 'read-tree', 'HEAD'],
                     ['git', 'hash-object', '-w', 'README_POLICY.md'],
                     ['git', 'archive', '-oowned.tar', 'HEAD'],
                     ['git', '-c', 'alias.unowned=!touch unowned', 'unowned']):
            result = run(args, root, env)
            assert result['status'] == 2 and result['stderr'].startswith('readonly epoch replay: Git command refused: ')
            controls.append({'name': 'refused-' + '-'.join(args[1:]), 'actual': result})
        foreign = run(['git', '-C', '..', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], root, env)
        assert foreign['status'] == 2 and foreign['stderr'] == 'readonly epoch replay: foreign Git working root\n'
        controls.append({'name': 'foreign-working-root', 'actual': foreign})
        calls = (root / '.artifacts/readonly-git-calls.jsonl').read_text()
        private_index = identity((root / '.artifacts/epoch.index').read_bytes())
        for name, action in (
            ('root-wildcard', lambda: epoch.scope(['.'])),
            ('missing-scope', lambda: epoch.scope([])),
            ('duplicate-scope', lambda: epoch.scope(['README_POLICY.md', 'README_POLICY.md'])),
            ('path-escape', lambda: epoch.safe_path('../escaped')),
            ('absolute-path', lambda: epoch.safe_path('/escaped')),
            ('metadata-path', lambda: epoch.safe_path('.git/config')),
            ('alias-escape', lambda: epoch.alias_target('README_POLICY.md', '../escaped')),
        ):
            try:
                action()
            except ValueError as error:
                controls.append({'name': name, 'cause': str(error)})
            else:
                raise ValueError('false-green control: ' + name)
        for name, member_name, oid in (('member-loss', 'unknown.txt', rows['README_POLICY.md']['oid']),
                                       ('blob-substitution', 'README_POLICY.md', '0' * 40)):
            child = root / name
            child.mkdir()
            member = tarfile.TarInfo(member_name)
            member.size = 1
            declared = {'README_POLICY.md': {'mode': '100644', 'oid': oid}}
            try:
                epoch.restore(member, io.BytesIO(b'x'), child, declared)
            except ValueError as error:
                controls.append({'name': name, 'cause': str(error)})
            else:
                raise ValueError('false-green control: ' + name)
    controls.append(blocked_control)
    after = primary()
    assert before == after
    proof = {'scope': 'Explicit small preparation population only; complete dated replay/current publication remains successor-owned. Logical historical path-size sum is not .git size or corruption evidence; whole-tree recovery was retired before copying.',
             'revision': epoch.REVISION, 'names': NAMES, 'metadata_base64': base64.b64encode(metadata).decode(),
             'objects': objects, 'rows': rows, 'recovered': recovered,
             'primary_before': before, 'primary_after': after, 'private_index': private_index,
             'positives': positives, 'controls': controls, 'accepted_calls': calls,
             'sources': {name: (BASE / name).read_text() for name in SOURCES}}
    (BASE / 'proof.json').write_text(json.dumps(proof, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('PASS explicit same-volume preparation, exact object/mode/alias recovery and read-only Git controls; full replay remains open.')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Independently consume exact native preparation evidence and genuine controls."""
import base64
import copy
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path('docs/audits/coordinate-public-final-preparation-20261008')
REVISION = 'a2840582fc1722c29da808713d6f3c06bd42cd78'
NAMES = ['README_POLICY.md', 'docs/book/src/reference-source/README_POLICY.markdown.source.txt',
         'scripts/check_docs_relative_paths.sh']
SCOPE = 'Explicit small preparation population only; complete dated replay/current publication remains successor-owned. Logical historical path-size sum is not .git size or corruption evidence; whole-tree recovery was retired before copying.'


def need(ok, cause):
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(cause)


def native(args):
    result = subprocess.run(['git', '--no-replace-objects', *args], capture_output=True)
    need(result.returncode == 0 and not result.stderr, 'complete independent native source')
    return result.stdout


def pin(raw):
    return {'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}


def check(proof):
    need(proof['revision'] == REVISION and proof['names'] == NAMES and proof['scope'] == SCOPE,
         'closed explicit preparation scope')
    need(proof['sources'] == {name: (BASE / name).read_text() for name in
         ('epoch.py', 'git_readonly.py', 'qualify.py', 'verify.py')}, 'complete preparation programme currency')
    raw = native(['--literal-pathspecs', 'ls-tree', '-r', '--full-tree', '-z', REVISION, '--', *NAMES])
    need(base64.b64decode(proof['metadata_base64'], validate=True) == raw, 'complete source metadata')
    rows = {}
    for record in raw.rstrip(b'\0').split(b'\0'):
        header, path = record.split(b'\t')
        mode, kind, oid = header.decode().split()
        need(kind == 'blob', 'published blob source')
        rows[path.decode()] = {'mode': mode, 'oid': oid}
    need(proof['rows'] == rows and set(rows) == set(NAMES) and set(proof['recovered']) == set(NAMES),
         'complete declared source membership')
    expected_objects = {}
    for path, row in rows.items():
        content = native(['show', REVISION + ':' + path])
        expected_objects[row['oid']] = base64.b64encode(content).decode()
        record = proof['recovered'][path]
        need(record['identity'] == pin(content) and type(record['identity']['bytes']) is int
             and record['mode'] == row['mode'] and record['same_volume'] is True
             and record['executable'] is (row['mode'] != '100644'), 'exact source bytes mode and same-volume recovery')
    need(proof['objects'] == expected_objects, 'complete native object bytes')
    alias = native(['show', REVISION + ':' + NAMES[1]]).decode()
    need(alias == '../../../../README_POLICY.md', 'published contained canonical alias')
    need(proof['primary_before'] == proof['primary_after'] and
         set(proof['primary_before']['files']) == {'index', 'config', 'HEAD', 'packed-refs'},
         'observed primary index configuration and reference conservation')
    positives = proof['positives']
    need(len(positives) == 5 and all(type(p['status']) is int and p['status'] == 0 and p['stderr'] == '' for p in positives[:4]),
         'typed actual positive statuses')
    need(positives[0]['arguments'] == ['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD']
         and len(positives[0]['stdout'].strip()) == 40
         and positives[1]['arguments'] == ['git', 'show', REVISION + ':README_POLICY.md']
         and positives[1]['stdout'] == native(['show', REVISION + ':README_POLICY.md']).decode(), 'complete actual object reader')
    expected_index = b''.join((row['mode'] + ' ' + row['oid'] + ' 0\t' + path).encode() + b'\0'
                             for path, row in sorted(rows.items()))
    need(positives[2]['arguments'] == ['git', 'ls-files', '--stage', '-z', '--', *NAMES]
         and positives[2]['stdout'].encode() == expected_index, 'complete private-index source identities')
    need(positives[3]['arguments'] == ['git', '-C', 'docs/book', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel']
         and Path(positives[3]['stdout'].strip()).name.startswith('coordinate-epoch-preparation-'),
         'owned nested Git working root')
    ignored = positives[4]
    need(ignored['arguments'] == ['git', 'check-ignore', '--no-index', '--stdin']
         and type(ignored['status']) is int and ignored['status'] == 1
         and ignored['stdout'] == ignored['stderr'] == '', 'native admitted source ignore policy')
    calls = [json.loads(line) for line in proof['accepted_calls'].splitlines()]
    need([r['arguments'] for r in calls] == [r['arguments'][1:] for r in positives]
         and [r['operation'] for r in calls] == ['rev-parse', 'show', 'ls-files', 'rev-parse', 'check-ignore'], 'closed actually accepted read operations')
    controls = proof['controls']
    need(len(controls) == 16 and len({c['name'] for c in controls}) == 16, 'complete genuine refusal population')
    for control in controls[:5]:
        actual = control['actual']
        need(type(actual['status']) is int and actual['status'] == 2 and actual['stdout'] == ''
             and actual['stderr'].startswith('readonly epoch replay: Git command refused: '), 'actual Git mutation refusals')
    foreign = controls[5]['actual']
    need(controls[5]['name'] == 'foreign-working-root' and type(foreign['status']) is int
         and foreign['status'] == 2 and foreign['stdout'] == ''
         and foreign['stderr'] == 'readonly epoch replay: foreign Git working root\n', 'foreign working-root refusal')
    need({c['name']: c['cause'] for c in controls[6:]} == {
        'root-wildcard': 'contained canonical source path',
        'missing-scope': 'explicit nonempty unique recovery scope',
        'duplicate-scope': 'explicit nonempty unique recovery scope',
        'path-escape': 'contained canonical source path',
        'absolute-path': 'contained canonical source path',
        'metadata-path': 'contained canonical source path',
        'alias-escape': 'contained canonical source path',
        'member-loss': 'archive source membership',
        'blob-substitution': 'whole source blob identity',
        'fixture-metadata-alias': 'fresh plain fixture metadata directory'}, 'complete intended recovery refusal causes')


def main():
    proof = json.loads((BASE / 'proof.json').read_bytes())
    check(proof)
    first = json.loads((BASE / 'first-reader-result.json').read_bytes())
    first_proof = json.loads(gzip.decompress((BASE / 'first-proof.json.gz').read_bytes()))
    need(type(first['status']) is int and first['status'] == 1 and first['stdout'] == ''
         and first['stderr'].endswith('ValueError: genuine result control\n')
         and first['source'] == first_proof['sources']['verify.py']
         and "need(candidate != proof, 'genuine result control')" in first['source'],
         'complete first Boolean-equality oracle failure')
    need(False == 0 and json.dumps(False) != json.dumps(0), 'typed Boolean/integer separation')
    controls = (
        ('missing-member', lambda p: p['recovered'].pop(NAMES[0]), 'complete declared source membership'),
        ('substituted-object', lambda p: p['objects'].update({p['rows'][NAMES[0]]['oid']: 'eA=='}), 'complete native object bytes'),
        ('Boolean-status', lambda p: p['positives'][0].update(status=False), 'typed actual positive statuses'),
        ('mutation-accepted', lambda p: p['controls'][0]['actual'].update(status=0), 'actual Git mutation refusals'),
        ('primary-change', lambda p: p['primary_after'].update(refs='changed'), 'observed primary index configuration and reference conservation'),
        ('full-replay-promotion', lambda p: p.update(scope='whole public replay qualified'), 'closed explicit preparation scope'),
    )
    for name, mutate, cause in controls:
        candidate = copy.deepcopy(proof)
        mutate(candidate)
        need(json.dumps(candidate, sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(proof, sort_keys=True), 'genuine result control')
        try:
            check(candidate)
        except ValueError as error:
            need(str(error) == cause, 'intended independent refusal: ' + name)
        else:
            raise ValueError('false-green independent control: ' + name)
    print('PASS complete explicit preparation evidence and independent hostile controls; full dated replay/current publication remains open.')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
